title: Best Books for RRB NTPC & Group D 2026: Subject-Wise
meta_description: Best books for RRB NTPC and Group D 2026. Lucent GK, RS Aggarwal quant & reasoning, Kiran PYQs. Subject-wise railway exam booklist with buying tips.

hero.one_liner: A focused railway exam booklist for RRB NTPC and Group D. Maths, reasoning, and general awareness with one main book per section.

intro: RRB NTPC and Group D test Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Awareness with General Science. The booklists overlap heavily, so one set covers both.
Railway exams reward broad general awareness and fast, accurate maths. Lucent for GK plus standard quant and reasoning books form the core.
Keep it lean: one main book per section, heavy previous year paper practice, and regular mock tests. Most of the syllabus overlaps with SSC, so SSC books work too.

buying_tips: If you already prepared for SSC, most of your maths, reasoning, and GK books work for railways too.
Lucent GK and General Science are inexpensive and high-yield; revise them repeatedly.
Spend more time on Kiran previous year papers than on buying new books. Railways repeats patterns heavily.

faqs.question: Are RRB NTPC and Group D books the same?
faqs.answer:
Largely yes. Both test maths, reasoning, and general awareness with science, so one set covers both.

Group D is slightly easier, but the same books prepare you for both.

faqs.question: Which is the best GK book for railway exams?
faqs.answer:
Lucent General Knowledge is the standard, paired with Lucent General Science.

Revise both several times, since the awareness section is large in railway exams.

faqs.question: Can SSC books be used for railway exams?
faqs.answer:
Yes, around 70% of the syllabus overlaps, especially maths, reasoning, and GK.

If you prepared for SSC CGL, you already own most of what you need.

faqs.question: How important are previous year papers for RRB?
faqs.answer:
Very important. Railways repeats question patterns heavily, so PYQs are high-yield.

Kiran's previous year papers are the most commonly used for this.

faqs.question: Do I need separate books for general science?
faqs.answer:
Lucent General Science is enough for the basic physics, chemistry, and biology that railway exams ask.

It is inexpensive and directly aligned with the exam level.

faqs.question: Is RS Aggarwal enough for railway maths?
faqs.answer:
For the base, yes. Add Rajesh Verma's Fast Track Objective Arithmetic for speed and shortcuts.

Then move to timed previous year papers and mocks.

faqs.question: How many books do I need for RRB NTPC?
faqs.answer:
About six to eight: one maths, one reasoning, Lucent GK, Lucent Science, and PYQ books.

Keep it lean and revise rather than collecting more.

faqs.question: Should I buy books in Hindi or English for railways?
faqs.answer:
Choose your comfortable language; Lucent and most standard books are available in both.

Railway exams are offered in many languages, so your medium is not a disadvantage.
